stories.title: US / Israel – Iran
stories.detail: Above its own baseline: 10 headlines against a normal of 31.5, and new language today (troops). That is a change, not just continuing coverage.
stories.why: The one flashpoint that hits gold through every channel at once. Safe-haven bid on the headline, Treasuries bid so nominal and real yields fall, and - uniquely - a credible threat to the Strait of Hormuz spikes crude, which lifts inflation expectations. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil passes through that strait.
stories.counterweight: The dollar is also a haven, so risk-off bids the dollar too and cancels part of gold's gain. This is why some escalation days produce a far smaller gold move than the headlines imply.
stories.duration: Days. Gold spikes on the exchange of fire and gives most of it back within a week unless the oil disruption is real and sustained, because only then does it reach the Fed's reaction function.
stories.spoken: Iran, and the US and Israel
stories.spoken_why: It reaches gold through three channels at once: the haven bid, lower real yields, and the risk to oil coming through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.read: Mostly not following - WTI crude, VIX, S&P 500 and 3 others are all going the other way. Either this is already in the price, or something bigger is driving the tape today.

stories.title: China / Taiwan
stories.detail: Coverage is below its own normal and carrying de-escalation language. Any risk premium here should be fading.
stories.why: Low frequency, very high severity. A genuine blockade or invasion scenario is the largest single tail risk in the gold market, because it would be a global supply-chain and reserve-currency event simultaneously.
stories.counterweight: Routine incursions and drills are so frequent they carry almost no information. Gold ignores them, correctly.
stories.duration: Drills: nothing. A real blockade: a regime change in gold pricing, not a spike.
stories.spoken_why: Routine drills mean nothing, but a genuine blockade would be the largest single risk in this market.
stories.read: Broadly consistent, though Gold, USD/JPY, Bitcoin and 2 others are not playing along. One asset out of line is usually its own story; several is a reason to doubt the read.

affairs.caveat: Expected direction is derived from the driver model; observed is what prices have actually done. Many things move at once, so this is a consistency check rather than attribution.

asia.read: Asian equities are mixed, averaging +0.36% - no clear overnight lead for London. Gold moved +1.76% overnight in a 1.96% range, and comes into London near the top of it. Holding the highs into the European open more often extends than fades, though a thin Asian range is weak evidence either way. 4 minor Asian releases overnight, none of them the kind that reaches gold.
asia.caveat: Measured from 00:00 UK to 14:06. Tokyo closes around 07:00 UK and Hong Kong around 09:00, so this is a session finishing rather than one that has finished.

correlations.regime: Gold and the dollar are running at -0.45. That is the textbook inverse relationship, so dollar moves are doing real work on the price. Against the S&P it is +0.34. Gold is trading WITH risk assets rather than against them, so it is behaving as a liquidity asset right now, not a hedge - do not rely on it to offset an equity drawdown while that holds.

flashpoints.name: Trade and tariffs
flashpoints.spoken_why: Tariffs raise prices and slow growth at the same time, which is the hardest combination for the Federal Reserve to answer.
flashpoints.why_gold: Indirect but real. Tariffs are an inflation impulse and a growth drag at once, which is the hardest combination for the Fed and therefore raises uncertainty about the rate path.
flashpoints.counterweight: Also dollar-positive in the short run, which works against gold. The net effect is genuinely ambiguous and often small.
flashpoints.typical_duration: Weeks, when it changes the inflation outlook. Announcement headlines alone rarely stick.
flashpoints.escalation_markers: Rates above expectations, retaliation, or extension to critical minerals and energy.

profile.name: FOMC Member Speaks
profile.what: Remarks from a regional Fed president or governor.
profile.why_gold: Mostly background, but a known hawk turning dovish - or the reverse - is a genuine signal, and voting members matter more than non-voters.
profile.watch: Whether the speaker votes this year, and whether they are departing from their usual stance.
profile.gotchas: Several speakers a day is normal and almost always noise. Treat as background unless the tone genuinely shifts.
